scene_summary: A small tiled room with a bed, white shelving and cabinet, two floor lamps, an open door, and a large white structure on the right.
overall_evidence: The reconstruction retains the main furniture group and tiled walls, but the viewpoint and framing differ substantially, the open door is reduced to a narrow strip, and prominent floor textures and warm illumination are missing. The right-hand structure also has a noticeably different visible silhouette.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction uses a much wider, more distant view, exposing the full bed and large areas of floor and a dark exterior border instead of the reference's tight, foreground-cropped composition.
main_defects.evidence: The reference bed extends beyond the bottom edge, whereas the reconstruction shows the entire bed within a smaller room view surrounded by dark background.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent changes in object spacing and size may result from the different viewpoint rather than actual layout errors.

main_defects.description: The broad, visibly paneled wooden door leaf is represented as a narrow plain vertical strip, losing its prominent face and panel detailing.
main_defects.evidence: A wide light-wood door with several inset panels dominates the reference center-right; only a thin pale door-like surface is visible in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: The narrower appearance could partly reflect a different camera angle or door opening angle.

main_defects.description: The reference's contrasting tan mottled floor covering and pale curved rug area are largely absent, leaving a nearly uniform gray floor.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a prominent brown irregularly patterned area behind the bed and a light curved patch near the doorway; the reconstruction shows mostly flat gray flooring with a small pale patch by the bed.
main_defects.uncertainty: The exact identity and full extent of these floor coverings are not clear from the reference.

main_defects.description: The large white structure on the right reads as a simple upright rectangular panel in the reconstruction, rather than the reference's foreground panel with a distinct raised, sloping white section behind it.
main_defects.evidence: The reference shows a slanted upper contour and overlapping white surfaces, while the reconstruction is dominated by one flat rectangular face and a small side projection.
main_defects.uncertainty: The object is cropped in the reference, so its identity and hidden construction cannot be established; viewpoint may affect its apparent silhouette.

main_defects.description: The warm, bright lamp glow and pronounced pools of light on the back wall are missing in the reconstruction, which is more uniformly gray and dim.
main_defects.evidence: The reference back lamp produces distinct warm highlights above and beside its shade; the corresponding reconstruction wall has no comparable glow.
main_defects.uncertainty: Exposure and rendering differences may contribute to the perceived change.

strengths: The bed, open shelving, small glazed cabinet, two slender floor lamps, doorway, and large white right-hand structure are all visibly represented.
The shelving and cabinet remain adjacent along the back wall, with a lamp near either side of the furniture group.
Pale grid-tiled walls, white furniture, and a light mattress on a beige bed base broadly match the reference's main visual elements.
uncertainty: This is a coarse initial automated visual judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. The images differ substantially in camera framing and lighting, making some apparent geometry and layout differences ambiguous. Occluded or cropped geometry is not evaluated.
